Hi team,

ClearBridge shared the Gulliver9b weights yesterday and product wants us to treat this as a high-priority intake due to a pilot next month. Quick summary of asks:

- Run compatibility checks (tokenizer, KV cache, attention patterns) and flag any non-backwards-compatible behaviors.
- Recommend a rollout strategy and whether we should apply a temporary version pin on hosted traffic until canary completes.
- Surface any infra capacity or routing constraints for a controlled canary.

I've attached the initial test matrix from the account (gulliver9b_test_matrix.xlsx). Sam — thanks for sending over sample prompts.

Immediate questions for engineering/research: how risky is the tokenizer change? If there's a non-trivial tokenization delta we should probably pin older variant for all production customers until we confirm prefix/embedding stability.

Can we get a short write-up of compatibility risks by EOD Thursday so I can update the pilot MRP?

Thanks,
Marissa

On 2028-06-12 09:03, Marissa Cole wrote:
> ClearBridge shared the Gulliver9b weights yesterday and product wants us to treat this as a high-priority intake due to a pilot next month.

Thanks for the signal. Quick technical read: initial tokenization pass shows differences on ~0.4% of tokens compared with our baseline tokenizer (edge cases around URLs, long hyphenated tokens). I've attached a small patch (tokenizer-diff.patch) and a script to reproduce.

Concrete risks:
- Embedding drift for prefix-based caching could cause cache miss spikes for a subset of customer prompts.
- Some legacy prompts that rely on token offsets (internal tooling) may see shifted spans — affects rerankers that use exact token positions.

Mitigations we can apply quickly:
1) Apply a temporary pin that routes ClearBridge pilot traffic to "gulliver9b-legacy-tokenizer" variant until our tokenizer shim is verified.
2) Add short-lived prefix caching bypass for that pilot (costly, but reduces correctness risk).

I'll run a 10k-sample regression by EOD and post results to the shared drive. If we decide to pin, infra may need 24-36h to prepare variant routing rules.

- Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tokenizer-diff.patch (diff), reproduce_tokenization.sh

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Gulliver9b integration: intake questions & temporary pin request

Thanks — ran evals on the 10k sample set Dev mentioned. High-level findings (summary attached as gulliver9b_eval_summary.pdf):

- Perplexity: modest improvement over baseline on SQuAD-like prompts.
- Instruction following: parity on short prompts, small regressions on multi-turn context >1024 tokens.
- Embedding cosine similarity vs baseline: mean shift of 0.012 (some drift in rare tokens).

Recommendation:
- Use gulliver9b-quant-v1 for production canary (keeps performance but reduces memory). This variant has equivalent tokenization to our shim — avoids the 0.4% token boundary cases.
- If we cannot ship the shim immediately, pin production traffic from ClearBridge (and any co-tenanted pilot groups) to gulliver9b-legacy-tokenizer until we complete a 72-hour canary.

Notes for SRE/Infra: the quant variant increases CPU decoding cost by ~8% in our profiling but reduces GPU memory by ~20%.

I'll upload full eval tables to the drive and include the prompt set used.

— Priyom
Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: gulliver9b_eval_summary.pdf

Appreciate the heads-up. Operational items to note:

- Routing: Implementing a temporary pin for ClearBridge requires a policy entry and a small canary pool. We can provision a 4-GPU canary cluster in Dedicated for the pilot, but that needs confirmation by EOD tomorrow to hit the pilot window.
- Telemetry: Can we add these two custom metrics for the canary: tokenization_mismatch_rate and prefix_cache_hit_rate? We need them in the per-route dashboard.
- SLA exception: If the pilot opts for prefix cache bypass we should temporarily relax the latency SLO for that route — bypass will increase p95 by ~30-50ms. We'll need a written approval for the exception.

Action items for Marissa/Sofia: confirm whether the pilot is allowed to accept the above latency delta and whether we want to use the quantized variant for the initial canary. If Marissa confirms, infra will start provisioning and I'll file a temporary routing rule change (HBSP-4627).

-Karthik

Thanks everyone — consolidating next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Decision (interim):
- Apply a temporary pin for the ClearBridge pilot traffic to gulliver9b-legacy-tokenizer for first 72-hour canary. This minimizes correctness risk while we verify shim.
- Run the canary on gulliver9b-quant-v1 internally for 48 hours in the dedicated canary cluster to validate perf/latency. If metrics look good, promote quant-v1 and decommission the legacy pin.

Action items & owners:
- Dev: finalize tokenizer shim reproduction and post the pass/fail artifacts to the Drive by 2028-06-14 14:00. (Will inform routing)
- Priyom: expand eval to 50k prompts focused on multi-turn >1024 tokens; share results by 2028-06-15 EOD.
- Karthik: provision 4-GPU canary cluster and create routing rule HBSP-4627; expose tokenization_mismatch_rate and prefix_cache_hit_rate in console by 2028-06-14 18:00.
- Marissa: confirm with ClearBridge whether they accept a temporary latency delta (we should have written acceptance) and coordinate pilot kickoff.

Sam — can you confirm in writing (reply-all) that ClearBridge accepts the 72-hour pinned pilot to the legacy tokenizer and understands potential short-term latency variance? We'll hold the routing change until we have that acknowledgement.

I'll keep this thread as the canonical intake. If anyone needs an async follow-up, paste to HBSP-4627.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
